articles.content_html:
RIYADH, Saudi Arabia — Saudi artificial intelligence company HUMAIN, backed by the Public Investment Fund, has introduced its first enterprise-grade personal computer, the Horizon Ultra, at the LEAP 2026 technology conference. The device, developed over a 12-month period in collaboration with Qualcomm, marks a notable transition for the domestic technology sector. The introduction of this hardware indicates a strategic shift for Saudi Arabia, moving the nation from its traditional role as a consumer of imported computing technology toward the design and development of end-user hardware tailored for the artificial intelligence era [1].

The Horizon Ultra is built around the Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Elite platform. This processor architecture enables the system to perform up to 80 trillion artificial intelligence operations per second locally. By handling intensive computational tasks directly on the device rather than relying exclusively on cloud infrastructure, the hardware addresses key enterprise concerns regarding data privacy, latency, and operational security. This capability is particularly relevant for corporate and government clients who require strict control over sensitive information while deploying advanced machine learning models in their daily workflows.

The launch at LEAP 2026 reflects broader efforts to establish a domestic hardware ecosystem capable of supporting advanced computing requirements. The 12-month development cycle undertaken with Qualcomm demonstrates a focused approach to bringing competitive enterprise hardware to market. This initiative aligns with regional economic diversification goals, emphasizing the creation of intellectual property and high-value technology products within the Kingdom. The resulting device is positioned to compete in an enterprise sector that is increasingly prioritizing dedicated hardware for artificial intelligence applications.

Agentic Interface and Hardware Integration

A central element of HUMAIN's strategy for the Horizon Ultra involves fundamentally rethinking the user interface. Rather than relying entirely on a conventional application-based operating environment, the system is designed to facilitate an "agentic AI" approach [2]. This model focuses on understanding and executing user intent across multiple applications and services simultaneously, rather than requiring the user to manually navigate discrete software programs. The objective is to streamline complex enterprise workflows, allowing the machine to autonomously manage routine tasks and data processing based on high-level instructions.

The hardware configuration, specifically the integration of the Snapdragon X2 Elite, provides the necessary local processing capacity to support this intent-driven interface. Executing an agentic operating model requires continuous, real-time analysis of user behavior and system context, which demands substantial computational resources. The ability to perform 80 trillion operations per second locally ensures that these background processes do not compromise overall system performance or require constant, high-bandwidth cloud connectivity. This localized processing approach is intended to provide a more responsive and secure user experience for enterprise clients.

The development of this hardware and software combination represents a significant technical undertaking. Integrating an advanced processor with an operating system designed around artificial intelligence requires extensive optimization to balance performance, power consumption, and thermal management. The collaboration with Qualcomm has likely focused heavily on these integration challenges, ensuring that the Horizon Ultra can maintain high levels of performance during sustained computational workloads typical of enterprise environments. The resulting system is intended to provide a robust platform for organizations seeking to integrate artificial intelligence more deeply into their operational processes.

Operating System Strategy and Market Rollout

HUMAIN has adopted a phased approach for the software ecosystem of the Horizon Ultra, expanding its strategic collaboration with Microsoft for the initial launch phase [1]. When the device becomes available for enterprise purchase on September 20, 2026, it will operate on the Windows platform [3]. This decision ensures immediate compatibility with existing corporate information technology infrastructure, allowing businesses to integrate the new hardware without disrupting their current software deployments or security protocols. Launching with a familiar operating system mitigates adoption friction for early enterprise customers.

Following this initial phase, HUMAIN plans to transition the Horizon Ultra to its own proprietary agentic artificial intelligence operating system in 2027. This bespoke software infrastructure is being developed to fully exploit the hardware's capabilities and realize the company's vision of an intent-driven computing environment. Developing a new operating system presents substantial technical and commercial challenges, including the need to build a comprehensive developer ecosystem and ensure compatibility with critical third-party enterprise applications. The success of this transition will be a critical factor in the long-term viability of HUMAIN's hardware platform.

The phased software strategy provides HUMAIN with a critical window to refine its proprietary operating system while simultaneously establishing a hardware footprint in the enterprise market. By securing early adoption through the Windows ecosystem, the company can gather valuable usage data and feedback from corporate clients. This information will likely be instrumental in optimizing the performance and functionality of the custom operating system ahead of its planned release in 2027. The ability to execute this transition smoothly will be closely monitored by industry analysts and enterprise technology leaders.

Regional Expansion and Future Implications

The commercial strategy for the Horizon Ultra includes an ambitious regional expansion plan. HUMAIN has established a target of deploying one million artificial intelligence personal computers across the Middle East and Africa by 2030. Achieving this volume will require significant investment in manufacturing capacity, supply chain logistics, and regional distribution networks. The company will also need to demonstrate clear return on investment for enterprise clients to drive large-scale procurement decisions in a competitive hardware market.

The successful deployment of domestic enterprise hardware on this scale would have substantial implications for the regional technology sector. It would establish a precedent for high-value hardware design and manufacturing within the Middle East, potentially attracting further investment and talent to the local ecosystem. Furthermore, providing regional enterprises with localized hardware designed specifically for artificial intelligence workloads could accelerate the adoption of advanced technologies across various sectors, from finance and healthcare to logistics and public administration.

As the September 2026 availability date approaches, the focus will shift to the practical performance of the Horizon Ultra in real-world enterprise environments. The device's ability to deliver on its stated performance metrics while maintaining reliability and security will be crucial for securing early enterprise contracts. The subsequent rollout of the proprietary operating system in 2027 will represent the next major test of HUMAIN's technical capabilities and strategic vision. The introduction of the Horizon Ultra at LEAP 2026 clearly signals an intent to compete in the global enterprise hardware market, marking a new phase in the development of the Saudi digital economy.

articles.content_html:
WE Solutions and Movandi announced a strategic partnership at LEAP 2026 in Riyadh to accelerate the deployment of advanced wireless connectivity technologies across Saudi Arabia. The collaboration, established via a Memorandum of Understanding on August 31, 2026, combines Movandi’s millimeter-wave (mmWave), RF semiconductor, beamforming, smart repeater, and software-defined networking technologies with WE Solutions’ local engineering, systems integration, cybersecurity, and project-delivery capabilities.

This strategic alignment is designed to help customers in the Kingdom transition rapidly from technology evaluation to real-world implementation. The targeted sectors include telecommunications, government, giga-projects, transport, enterprise, and critical infrastructure environments. By focusing on the integration and deployment enablement of next-generation wireless systems, the partnership addresses the growing demand for high-performance connectivity in the region.

Enabling Advanced Wireless Infrastructure

The deployment of advanced wireless systems requires specialized expertise and robust technology. Movandi’s mmWave and RF technologies provide the foundational hardware and software necessary for high-capacity, low-latency networks. When integrated by WE Solutions, these technologies can be customized to meet the specific requirements of Saudi Arabia's diverse sectors. The collaboration aims to overcome the technical challenges associated with deploying advanced wireless infrastructure, such as signal propagation and network optimization.

According to the announcement, the partnership will leverage WE Solutions' local presence and integration capabilities to deliver tailored solutions. articles.content_html:
RIYADH, Saudi Arabia — A strong delegation of Pakistan tech firms is targeting the Saudi digital economy with specialized solutions at LEAP 2026, marking a concerted effort to establish a deeper foothold in the Kingdom's rapidly expanding technology sector. The initiative, anchored by a dedicated pavilion featuring 20 technology companies, is formally supported by the Pakistan Software Export Board and the Trade Development Authority of Pakistan. Pakistan's IT Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja is attending the prominent Riyadh tech event to inaugurate the pavilion and deliver a keynote address, underscoring the strategic importance of the Saudi market to Pakistan's technology export ambitions.

The presence of these companies at LEAP 2026 highlights a shift from exploratory visits to concrete cross-border expansion strategies. Following successful participation in previous iterations of the event, returning firms are translating initial engagements into permanent operational bases. KAACIB, a notable participant in LEAP 2025, is leveraging its prior success by opening a local office in Riyadh, a move that signals long-term commitment to the Saudi tech ecosystem and a desire to capture a larger share of the enterprise software market in the region.

The delegation's composition reflects a strategic alignment with the core pillars of Saudi Vision 2030, particularly the emphasis on digital transformation, economic diversification, and the development of a robust knowledge-based economy. By bringing a diverse array of enterprise software, digital government solutions, and startup ecosystem expertise to the Kingdom, the participating companies are positioning themselves as capable partners in Saudi Arabia's ambitious modernization drive.

This sustained engagement is not merely transactional; it represents a fundamental shift in how Pakistani technology providers view the Middle East market. The establishment of local offices, such as the one announced by KAACIB, facilitates closer collaboration with Saudi clients, enables more responsive customer support, and allows for the customization of products to meet specific regional requirements. This localized approach is increasingly recognized as a prerequisite for success in a market characterized by rapid technological adoption and stringent regulatory standards.

Building on Previous Successes

The current push for Saudi Arabia expansion builds upon tangible business outcomes from previous engagements. According to data from the Pakistan Software Export Board, the country's participation in LEAP 2025 generated $9.74 million in business and resulted in 78 qualified leads. This track record of measurable return on investment has catalyzed increased participation and a more structured approach to market entry for the 2026 delegation. The focus has shifted toward delivering tailored solutions that address specific regulatory and operational requirements within the Kingdom.

The financial and operational metrics from the previous year serve as a compelling validation of the market potential for Pakistani technology firms in Saudi Arabia. The nearly $10 million in generated business demonstrates that Saudi enterprises are receptive to the specialized capabilities offered by these companies. Furthermore, the 78 qualified leads indicate a robust pipeline of future opportunities, providing a strong rationale for the expanded presence at the current iteration of the event.

This evolution is evident in the product offerings being showcased by the delegation. Rather than presenting generic enterprise solutions, these companies are demonstrating platforms that are deeply integrated with Saudi Arabia's digital infrastructure. The alignment with local standards is critical for securing enterprise and government contracts, as organizations in the Kingdom increasingly demand solutions that are natively compliant with national regulations and data sovereignty requirements.

The strategic support provided by the Pakistan Software Export Board and the Trade Development Authority of Pakistan has been instrumental in facilitating this market entry. By organizing a dedicated pavilion and providing logistical and marketing support, these government agencies are reducing the barriers to entry for participating companies. This collaborative approach between the public and private sectors is essential for building a sustainable technology export industry.

Tailoring Solutions for the Saudi Market

Among the newer entrants demonstrating specialized capabilities is Stellisys, which is showcasing a Saudi-specific version of its platform. A key feature of their offering is [ZATCA-compliant invoicing][1], demonstrating a clear understanding of the regulatory landscape governing digital transactions in the Kingdom. By integrating an artificial intelligence layer with local compliance requirements, Stellisys aims to address the complex needs of businesses operating in Saudi Arabia's logistics, real estate, and enterprise technology sectors.

The Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA) regulations represent a significant compliance hurdle for businesses operating in Saudi Arabia, and the ability to offer natively compliant solutions is a major competitive advantage. Stellisys's focus on this specific requirement highlights a sophisticated approach to product development that prioritizes local market needs over generic functionality. The integration of artificial intelligence capabilities further enhances the value proposition.

The focus on regulatory compliance and localized features reflects a broader trend among international technology providers seeking to establish a presence in the Middle East tech ecosystem. As Saudi Vision 2030 accelerates the digitization of the economy, the demand for sophisticated, compliant software solutions continues to grow. The Pakistani delegation's emphasis on tailored products positions them to compete effectively in a market that values both technological innovation and adherence to local standards.

The presence of companies specializing in logistics and supply chain management, geospatial technology, and digital government solutions further underscores the breadth of capabilities being offered by the delegation. These sectors are critical components of Saudi Arabia's economic diversification strategy, and the availability of specialized technology solutions will play a key role in driving efficiency and innovation across these industries.

Strategic Partnerships and Future Outlook

The inauguration of the pavilion by IT Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja highlights the government-level support for these tech partnerships. The coordinated effort between the Pakistan Software Export Board, the Trade Development Authority of Pakistan, and private sector participants like ByteCorp and KAACIB demonstrates a unified approach to international expansion. This collaborative model is designed to provide companies with the necessary backing to navigate the complexities of entering a new market and establishing sustainable operations.

While the immediate focus is on generating leads and securing contracts at LEAP 2026, the long-term objective is to build a permanent presence in the Kingdom. The opening of KAACIB's Riyadh office serves as a blueprint for other firms seeking to transition from event participants to established local entities. This physical expansion facilitates closer engagement with clients, enables the development of localized support infrastructure, and demonstrates a tangible commitment to the Saudi market.

However, the success of these expansion efforts will depend on the ability of these companies to continuously adapt their solutions to the evolving needs of the Saudi market and maintain compliance with future regulatory changes. The transition from initial market entry to sustained growth remains a significant challenge that will require ongoing investment in local talent and infrastructure. Companies must also navigate the competitive landscape of the Saudi technology sector, which is attracting significant investment from global players.

The outcomes of the 2026 delegation will provide valuable insights into the viability of the Pakistan-Saudi technology corridor. If the participating companies can successfully translate their event presence into sustainable business relationships, it will pave the way for increased collaboration and investment in the future. The continued support of government agencies and the ongoing commitment of private sector participants will be essential for realizing the full potential of this strategic partnership.

articles.content_html:
Blossom Accelerator has been named the Official Soft-Landing Partner for LEAP 2026 in Riyadh, creating a dedicated pathway for international startups to establish a presence in Saudi Arabia. The partnership, announced by the company and reflected in event programming, is designed to give vetted founders priority access to market-entry support, including licensing guidance and introductions to local programs that can accelerate setup and early operations. Blossom outlined the soft-landing track on its site and amplified the news on its X and Instagram channels, positioning the initiative squarely within LEAP 2026’s founder-facing agenda.

For startups weighing expansion into the Kingdom, the significance lies in the formalization of a process that has often been fragmented. According to Blossom Accelerator, the partner role consolidates regulatory navigation, early-stage operational support and access to government-linked programs into a single, structured route. That framing sets expectations around timing and deliverables, and gives founders a named point of accountability during a busy global tech gathering.

Streamlining the MISA Licensing Process

At the core of the pathway is licensing. Blossom’s program includes support to obtain the Ministry of Investment (MISA) Entrepreneurship Registration Certificate, a prerequisite for most foreign founders aiming to operate in Saudi Arabia. The accelerator says vetted companies using its route can often complete certification processing in about 30 days and, for qualifying startups, without initial processing costs. While individual timelines vary with case complexity, a one-month target meaningfully compresses what can otherwise be a multi-step onboarding with uncertain duration.

Licensing speed matters because market timing is an execution risk for early-stage teams. A predictable MISA process clarifies when a startup can begin contracting, hire local staff and open accounts. It also reduces the administrative overhead founders face when navigating new jurisdictions. In this case, Blossom is positioning itself as an official facilitator rather than a general advisor, an important distinction for teams prioritizing certainty around prerequisites and documentation.

Integration with NTDP Funding

The soft-landing track is also tied to potential non-dilutive funding. Blossom connects participating startups with programs under the National Technology Development Program (NTDP), including MVPLab and Transform+, which the accelerator says can offer grants and subsidies of up to 800,000 SAR. The integration does not guarantee awards, but it places qualified founders on a defined path to evaluate and apply for state-backed incentives that can underwrite localization, product adaptation and first customer acquisition.

For teams arriving from abroad, the pairing of regulatory facilitation with potential NTDP support addresses two common friction points: initial compliance costs and the cash gap between entry and early revenue. TechScoop analysis: when private accelerators act as named conduits to government programs, it can shorten discovery cycles for founders unfamiliar with the local funding landscape and reduce duplication of effort across agencies and service providers. The practical upside is less time spent mapping the system and more time calibrating go-to-market plans for Saudi customers.

Practical Guidance at LEAP 2026

The partnership will be visible on the ground during LEAP 2026. Blossom Founder and CEO Emon Shakoor is slated to lead a closed-door workshop focused on market entry and contracting in the Kingdom, with an emphasis on the mechanics of company setup, regulatory requirements and how to structure corporate partnerships. The session, listed in LEAP’s program as a partner event, is intended to move beyond high-level orientation and into checklists and sequencing for founders making near-term decisions about legal form, licensing and procurement pathways. Details for the session appear on the LEAP 2026 site.

Access to discrete, practitioner-led sessions can be the difference between a founder leaving an event with a pitch deck of generalities and a workable plan of action. In that context, the soft-landing role comes with a commitment to operational specificity. Blossom also describes “priority access” and “tailored support” for vetted participants on its program page, positioning the workshop as one component of a broader, time-bound sequence that begins at LEAP and continues through licensing and initial business development.

Blossom is not starting from zero. The accelerator says it has helped more than 100 businesses from 15 countries expand into Saudi Arabia, a history it cites as the basis for codifying a repeatable entry pathway. For international founders, that track record may offer some comfort on practical matters such as document preparation, typical roadblocks and the order in which to tackle tasks that, if mis-sequenced, can burn weeks.

There are, however, clear guardrails around the offer. The expedited MISA timeline is described as “often within 30 days,” which signals a target, not a guarantee; final durations still depend on official reviews and the completeness of each application. The “no initial cost” phrasing applies to vetted startups, so eligibility criteria and any subsequent fees or capital requirements will matter for teams budgeting their runway. Likewise, NTDP grants are competitive and subject to program rules; connection does not equate to approval, and founders should expect diligence on traction, local value-add and use of funds.

Capacity is another practical consideration. A closed-door workshop implies limited seats and the likelihood of pre-registration. Founders interested in the soft-landing track may need to engage with Blossom before or during LEAP 2026 to secure access to consultations, licensing support and introductions to NTDP program managers. In previous years, many founders have sought legal and accounting advice through fragmented channels; one test for this partnership will be whether it can triage demand without creating a new bottleneck at the point of intake.

For local service providers—law firms, corporate services shops and recruiters—the emergence of an official partner may reset expectations about the baseline of support available on-venue at LEAP. The arrangement does not replace private advisors, but it could standardize certain steps and documentation packets, making downstream engagements more efficient. Investors and corporate procurement teams may also benefit if licensing timelines become more predictable, shortening the gap between interest, vendor onboarding and first pilot.

The bigger picture is execution. As LEAP 2026 approaches, the effectiveness of the soft-landing pathway will be measured less by sign-ups and more by conversion: how many participating startups secure their MISA Entrepreneurship Registration Certificate on the expected timeline, how many proceed to file commercial registrations and open local bank accounts, and how many leverage MVPLab or Transform+ to reach first revenue. TechScoop analysis: a structured route reduces uncertainty, but it does not eliminate the core growth challenges that follow market entry—finding product–market fit with Saudi customers, hiring locally for sales and delivery, and building compliant data and contracting processes.

Blossom’s role gives international founders a clearer starting point, backed by official status at one of the region’s largest tech gatherings. The next checkpoint will come during LEAP 2026 itself, when the workshop convenes and the first cohort of participating startups begins moving through the sequence from orientation to licensing to early pilots. If the model delivers on the timelines and connections outlined on Blossom’s site and in LEAP’s session listing, it could set a template for how official event partners structure soft-landing programs across future editions.

articles.content_html:
In a coordinated push to connect emerging market startups with the Gulf's rapidly expanding digital economy, Builders Tribe and the Pakistan IT Industry Association (P@SHA) have organized dedicated founder delegations to LEAP 2026 in Riyadh. The organized efforts underscore the Saudi capital's growing role as a vital bridge for international tech investment, providing a structured pathway for African, global, and Pakistani entrepreneurs to access the GCC's thriving tech ecosystem. The move reflects a broader trend of emerging markets looking toward Saudi Arabia as a primary destination for technological collaboration and capital deployment.

The initiatives highlight a shift from general event attendance to highly targeted, cross-border business development. According to [Builders Tribe][1], its exclusive founder delegation is designed to connect entrepreneurs directly with the GCC startup ecosystem. The organization's focus centers on facilitating cross-border opportunities, particularly establishing links between Africa and the GCC in high-growth sectors such as financial technology and artificial intelligence. Simultaneously, [P@SHA][2] is bringing a focused delegation to showcase Pakistani IT capabilities, aiming to help local companies explore export opportunities and forge long-term partnerships in the Middle East.

Strategic Expansion into the GCC

The dual delegations arrive at a time when Saudi Arabia is actively seeking to diversify its economy and establish Riyadh as a central hub for global technology and innovation. For emerging market founders, the GCC represents a crucial source of capital and a lucrative market for enterprise software, fintech solutions, and AI applications. Builders Tribe's initiative is specifically structured to help African and global founders navigate this landscape, connecting them with regional investors and potential enterprise partners who can facilitate cross-border expansion. The delegation model provides a necessary framework for startups that might otherwise struggle to establish a foothold in a competitive and rapidly evolving regional market.

By organizing an exclusive delegation, Builders Tribe aims to provide its network of entrepreneurs with direct access to the decision-makers shaping the region's digital infrastructure. This structured approach to international expansion reflects a growing recognition that successful entry into the Middle East market requires localized partnerships and direct engagement with key stakeholders. The focus on fintech and AI aligns closely with the investment priorities currently dominating the Saudi digital economy, where both sectors are experiencing significant capital inflows and regulatory support designed to foster innovation and technological adoption. The organized delegation ensures that founders are positioned to capitalize on these specific sectoral opportunities.

Showcasing Pakistan's IT Capabilities

Parallel to the Builders Tribe initiative, the Pakistan IT Industry Association is utilizing LEAP 2026 delegations to position its domestic technology sector for international growth. P@SHA's delegation is focused on showcasing the technical capabilities of Pakistani IT companies to a global audience. The association's primary objective is to explore concrete business, investment, and partnership opportunities within the Middle East, leveraging the massive gathering of industry leaders in Riyadh. The effort represents a calculated strategy to increase the visibility of Pakistani technology solutions in a region that is actively investing in digital infrastructure and enterprise software modernization.

For Pakistani technology firms, the GCC market offers significant potential for IT service exports and enterprise software deployment. By participating as an organized delegation, these companies can present a unified front, demonstrating the maturity and capacity of Pakistan's tech sector to prospective clients and investors in Saudi Arabia and the broader Gulf region. The effort represents a strategic move to integrate Pakistani tech talent and solutions more deeply into the Middle East's digital transformation initiatives. This organized representation is particularly important for enterprise software providers seeking to establish credibility and trust with large regional corporations and government entities driving the digital agenda.

Bridging Emerging Markets and Middle East Tech Investment

Both the Builders Tribe and P@SHA delegations emphasize the critical importance of networking with international tech leaders, investors, and enterprise decision-makers at the Riyadh event. The presence of these organized groups at LEAP 2026 highlights the conference's function not just as an exhibition, but as a practical marketplace for Middle East tech investment and cross-border collaboration. The delegations serve as concentrated nodes of emerging market innovation, allowing investors to efficiently evaluate multiple opportunities within a structured environment.

For GCC investors and enterprise buyers, these delegations offer a curated selection of emerging market startups and IT service providers. Instead of navigating the vast global tech landscape independently, regional stakeholders can engage directly with vetted founders from Africa, Pakistan, and other emerging markets. This dynamic facilitates more efficient capital allocation and partnership formation, accelerating the integration of international innovation into the local ecosystem. The structured nature of the delegations also provides investors with a level of assurance regarding the quality and preparedness of the participating startups, streamlining the initial stages of due diligence and relationship building.

Looking Ahead

While the organization of these delegations marks a significant step in connecting emerging markets with the GCC, the ultimate measure of their success will be the volume of concrete partnerships and investments that materialize post-event. Navigating the regulatory and business environment in Saudi Arabia requires sustained effort beyond initial networking. The participating founders will need to translate the connections made at LEAP 2026 into actionable business agreements and localized operations. The ability to maintain momentum after the event concludes will be critical for the long-term success of the startups seeking to establish a permanent presence in the region.

Furthermore, the long-term impact of these initiatives will depend on the ability of the startups to adapt their solutions to the specific needs of the Middle Eastern market. As Builders Tribe and P@SHA guide their respective cohorts through the event, the focus will likely shift from initial introductions to detailed discussions on compliance, localization, and strategic alignment with Saudi Arabia's broader economic objectives. The delegations represent the beginning of a complex process of cross-border integration, where ongoing support and strategic navigation will be required to convert initial interest into sustainable commercial success within the GCC ecosystem.

articles.content_html:
Riyadh — QuikBot Technologies and Embed Financial Group Holdings (EFGH) have signed a Strategic Partnership Agreement to integrate real-time insurance directly into autonomous robotic systems. Announced ahead of LEAP 2026, the collaboration focuses on QuikBot's Ambient Permission Plane, ensuring that every action taken by an autonomous delivery robot is automatically insured dynamically at the point of action [1]. This QuikBot EFGH partnership addresses the liability bottleneck in scaling autonomous urban logistics, shifting the paradigm from static insurance policies to contextual, embedded protection for physical AI [1].

Embedding Protection into Physical AI

Under the agreement signed on March 2, 2026, EFGH will serve as the exclusive insurance partner for QuikBot’s Ambient Permission Plane [1]. This integration allows for real-time insurance coverage triggered by specific autonomous actions, such as a robot entering a building or completing a delivery [1]. The coverage includes public liability, cyber liability, product liability, property damage, and cargo-in-transit, providing comprehensive protection for autonomous systems in complex urban environments [1]. This ensures that every move the autonomous delivery robots make is covered dynamically at the point of action, rather than relying on traditional static policies [1].

According to the companies, this dynamic approach to insurance is designed to meet the unique challenges of deploying physical AI in public spaces. By embedding insurance directly into the operational workflow of autonomous robots, the partnership aims to streamline the deployment process and reduce the administrative burden associated with traditional, static insurance policies. The QuikBot EFGH partnership is a major step toward enabling seamless and secure operations for autonomous delivery robots [1].

Scaling Autonomous Urban Logistics

QuikBot Technologies, led by CEO Alan Ng, who is a featured speaker at LEAP 2026, has already deployed its autonomous delivery robots in key commercial sites in Singapore, including South Beach and Mapletree Business City [1]. These live deployments serve as a proving ground for the integration of real-time insurance into autonomous systems, demonstrating the viability of the Ambient Permission Plane in real-world scenarios [1]. The success of these initial deployments in Singapore provides a strong foundation for scaling the technology to other urban centers globally, demonstrating that dynamic insurance can effectively mitigate risks in densely populated areas [1].

The partnership with QuikBot expands EFGH's Finternet strategy into the realm of embedded insurance, highlighting the growing intersection of financial technology and physical AI [1]. As autonomous systems become more prevalent in urban logistics, the need for scalable and adaptable insurance solutions becomes increasingly critical. This shift highlights the importance of transitioning away from traditional models that are not designed for the rapid pace of technological innovation in physical AI. This collaboration represents a significant step towards addressing the liability bottleneck that has hindered the widespread adoption of autonomous delivery robots [1].

Implications for the Gulf Region

While the initial deployments are focused on Singapore, the implications of this partnership extend globally, particularly to regions like the Gulf, where smart city initiatives are rapidly advancing. In Saudi Arabia, for example, the development of futuristic urban projects and the broader Vision 2030 agenda creates a fertile ground for the adoption of autonomous logistics solutions. The integration of real-time insurance into these systems could accelerate their deployment in the region, providing a blueprint for other smart cities to follow.

The deployment of autonomous systems in complex urban environments requires a robust framework for managing risk and liability. The QuikBot EFGH partnership offers a potential solution to this challenge, providing a scalable and adaptable model for embedded insurance. As smart city initiatives continue to evolve in the Gulf region and beyond, the integration of physical AI and real-time insurance will likely play a crucial role in shaping the future of urban logistics.

Addressing the Liability Bottleneck

The liability bottleneck has long been a significant barrier to the widespread adoption of autonomous systems in urban environments. Traditional insurance models, which rely on static policies and historical data, are often ill-equipped to handle the dynamic and unpredictable nature of physical AI. By embedding real-time insurance directly into the operational workflow of autonomous robots, QuikBot and EFGH are addressing this challenge head-on.

This approach not only provides comprehensive coverage for a wide range of potential liabilities but also streamlines the deployment process, making it easier for companies to integrate autonomous systems into their operations. As the technology continues to mature and regulatory frameworks evolve, the integration of real-time insurance will likely become a standard feature of autonomous logistics solutions, paving the way for more efficient and sustainable urban environments.

However, the widespread adoption of this technology will depend on regulatory frameworks and the willingness of local authorities to embrace dynamic insurance models. As QuikBot and EFGH prepare to showcase their partnership at LEAP 2026 in Riyadh, the industry will be watching closely to see how this innovative approach to insurance for physical AI is received by stakeholders in the Middle East and beyond. The success of this partnership could have far-reaching implications for the future of autonomous systems and the broader integration of physical AI into everyday life. By addressing the critical issue of liability, QuikBot and EFGH are helping to unlock the full potential of autonomous urban logistics. This approach not only mitigates financial risks but also fosters greater trust among stakeholders, enabling a new era of efficiency and innovation in smart cities around the world.

articles.content_html:
U.S.-based AI infrastructure company Velaura AI has secured $110 million in a Series A funding round, propelling its valuation beyond the $1 billion mark. The substantial investment was led by Seligman Ventures and saw participation from prominent backers, including Saudi Aramco-backed Prosperity7 Ventures. This funding round underscores the surging global demand for energy-efficient AI computing solutions, as the rapid expansion of generative AI continues to drive up operating costs and place immense pressure on power grids worldwide. The announcement, made against the backdrop of discussions at DeepFest 2026 in Riyadh, highlights the strategic importance of sustainable computing in the region's technological roadmap.

The investment arrives at a critical juncture for the technology sector, where the computational requirements of advanced artificial intelligence models are outpacing the capabilities of traditional infrastructure. As companies race to develop and deploy generative AI applications, the corresponding surge in energy consumption has prompted urgent calls for more efficient hardware solutions. Velaura AI's successful funding round indicates strong investor confidence in its approach to solving this systemic challenge, positioning the company as a key player in the transition toward sustainable AI development. The infusion of capital will be instrumental in scaling the company's operations to meet the growing demands of a rapidly evolving market.

Addressing the Power Demands of AI

The newly acquired capital will primarily support the ongoing development and commercialization of Velaura AI's low-power computing technologies. At the heart of this effort is the company's proprietary Titan Core platform, an architecture specifically designed to dramatically improve the energy efficiency of AI accelerators. As organizations increasingly deploy complex AI models, the energy consumption of data centers has become a critical bottleneck. Velaura's approach aims to mitigate this challenge by delivering high-performance computing capabilities while significantly reducing power requirements. This architectural innovation is essential for sustaining the growth of AI without exacerbating environmental concerns.

The Titan Core technology has already achieved significant market penetration, being commercially deployed across more than 30 million ASIC chips. This widespread adoption demonstrates the viability and scalability of Velaura's solution in real-world applications. By optimizing the fundamental architecture of AI processors, the company is addressing one of the most pressing concerns in the tech industry today: balancing the insatiable demand for computing power with environmental and economic constraints. The deployment scale also provides Velaura with valuable real-world performance data, which will likely inform future iterations of the Titan Core architecture and further refine its efficiency metrics.

Furthermore, the focus on energy efficiency is not merely an environmental imperative but a fundamental economic necessity for data center operators. The rising costs of electricity, coupled with the immense cooling requirements of high-performance computing clusters, are squeezing profit margins across the industry. Velaura AI's technology promises to alleviate these pressures by offering a more favorable performance-per-watt ratio compared to conventional alternatives. This value proposition is expected to resonate strongly with cloud service providers and enterprise customers seeking to optimize their infrastructure expenditures while maintaining the computational throughput required for advanced AI workloads.

Expanding Applications to Physical AI

Beyond traditional data center applications, Velaura AI's technology is also heavily targeted at the emerging field of Physical AI. This domain encompasses robotics, drones, and other autonomous systems where computing performance must operate within exceptionally tight power and thermal constraints. In these environments, traditional high-power processors are often unsuitable due to battery limitations and heat dissipation challenges. The ability to execute complex AI algorithms efficiently at the edge is a critical enabler for the next generation of autonomous devices.

The Titan Core platform offers a compelling solution for these edge computing scenarios, enabling advanced AI capabilities in devices that require strict energy management. As the robotics industry continues to evolve, the demand for efficient on-device processing will only grow. Velaura's focus on this sector positions the company to capitalize on the increasing integration of AI into physical systems, from industrial automation to consumer electronics. The ability to process complex AI workloads locally, without relying on continuous cloud connectivity, is crucial for applications requiring real-time responsiveness and high reliability in unpredictable environments.

In the context of autonomous vehicles and advanced manufacturing robotics, the implications of energy-efficient computing are profound. These systems require continuous processing of vast amounts of sensor data to navigate complex environments safely and efficiently. By providing a low-power alternative for these computationally intensive tasks, Velaura AI is helping to unlock new possibilities in the deployment of autonomous technologies. The company's progress in this area will be closely watched by industry observers and potential partners seeking to leverage AI in resource-constrained environments where traditional computing paradigms fall short.

Strategic Investment and Future Outlook

The participation of Prosperity7 Ventures, the venture capital arm of Saudi Aramco, is particularly noteworthy. It reflects a broader strategic interest within the Middle East, and specifically Saudi Arabia, in fostering advanced technological capabilities. As the region diversifies its economy and invests heavily in digital infrastructure, partnerships with leading AI hardware innovators like Velaura AI are crucial. This investment aligns with the goals of initiatives discussed at DeepFest 2026, emphasizing the need for sustainable and scalable AI solutions to support the region's ambitious technological transformation. The collaboration could also open new avenues for Velaura to deploy its technology within the expansive industrial and energy sectors of the Middle East.

Looking ahead, Velaura AI plans to utilize the $110 million funding to significantly expand its engineering teams. This expansion will accelerate the refinement of the Titan Core platform and support the development of next-generation low-power computing technologies. While the company has demonstrated strong initial traction with its ASIC deployments, the challenge remains to maintain its competitive edge in a rapidly evolving market. The success of its commercialization efforts will depend on its ability to continually deliver superior energy efficiency metrics against established semiconductor giants and emerging startups alike. The company must navigate a complex landscape of competing architectures and evolving industry standards.

The infusion of capital also provides Velaura with the resources necessary to scale its operations and pursue new market opportunities. As the AI hardware landscape becomes increasingly competitive, the company will need to demonstrate sustained technological leadership and strong execution capabilities. The backing of prominent investors like Seligman Ventures and Prosperity7 provides a solid foundation for these efforts, but the ultimate test will be Velaura's ability to translate its innovative architecture into broad commercial success across diverse applications and industries. The coming years will be critical for the company as it seeks to establish its low-power computing technologies as a foundational element of the global AI infrastructure.

articles.content_html:
As LEAP 2026 prepares to host its fifth edition at the Riyadh Exhibition and Convention Center (RECC) Malham in Riyadh, the event has finalized its primary logistical partnerships to manage attendee mobility. Gulf Car has been named the official transportation provider for LEAP 2026, tasked with helping attendees travel directly to and from the venue. Complementing the external transit, Makani has been appointed as the official internal shuttle provider to facilitate effortless movement within the expansive exhibition grounds, ensuring attendees can navigate between sessions, activations, and meetings without delay.

This multi-tiered transport strategy addresses the significant logistical challenges of moving hundreds of thousands of visitors across the sprawling RECC Malham complex. The LEAP 2026 transportation plan aims to ensure seamless travel to, from, and within the venue, recognizing that efficient mobility is critical to the overall success of the event. The integration of these services reflects a comprehensive approach to managing the influx of participants expected to attend the technology gathering.

Official Transportation Partnerships

Gulf Car's appointment as the official transportation provider highlights the event organizers' commitment to providing reliable and accessible travel options for all participants. The company will manage external transit operations, offering a range of services designed to accommodate the diverse needs of attendees traveling to the RECC Malham venue in Riyadh. This partnership is a key component of the broader strategy to ensure that reaching the event is as straightforward as possible for both local and international visitors.

Makani, serving as the official internal shuttle provider, will focus on optimizing movement within the exhibition grounds. The scale of LEAP 2026 necessitates a robust internal transport system, and Makani's role is to ensure that attendees can easily transition between different areas of the event, maximizing their time and engagement with the various sessions and exhibits. The internal shuttles are expected to significantly reduce transit times between the numerous halls and activation zones.

Comprehensive Mobility Solutions

In addition to the primary partnerships with Gulf Car and Makani, corporate transport solutions like Swvl are offering dedicated delegate and group shuttles. These services include airport transfers and daily hotel-to-venue routes, providing a comprehensive mobility network for attendees. The integration of multiple transport providers underscores the complexity of managing logistics for an event of this magnitude, requiring precise coordination across various transit modes.

The collaborative approach to transportation for LEAP 2026 reflects a broader trend in the events industry, where specialized providers are engaged to handle specific aspects of the attendee experience. By dividing responsibilities between external transit, internal shuttles, and corporate transport, the organizers aim to create a cohesive and efficient mobility ecosystem. This structured division of labor allows each provider to focus on their core competencies, ultimately benefiting the attendees.

The appointment of Gulf Car as the official transportation provider is designed to streamline the journey for attendees heading to the Riyadh Exhibition and Convention Center (RECC) Malham. By securing a dedicated partner for external transit, the organizers of LEAP 2026 are addressing one of the primary logistical concerns associated with large-scale exhibitions. The focus on seamless travel to and from the venue is intended to minimize delays and enhance the overall experience for participants navigating the Riyadh metropolitan area.

Similarly, the role of Makani as the official internal shuttle provider is crucial for managing the flow of attendees within the expansive RECC Malham complex. The physical footprint of LEAP 2026 requires an efficient internal transport mechanism to ensure that visitors can move quickly between different sessions, exhibition halls, and meeting areas. Makani's internal shuttles are positioned to facilitate this movement, allowing attendees to maximize their engagement with the event's offerings without being hindered by long transit times across the venue.

The inclusion of Swvl in the transportation strategy adds another layer of mobility support, specifically catering to delegates and groups. By offering dedicated shuttles, including airport transfers and daily routes from hotels to the venue, Swvl provides a targeted solution for attendees requiring structured transport options. This component of the mobility plan is particularly relevant for international visitors and corporate groups, ensuring they have reliable transit arrangements throughout the duration of LEAP 2026.

The comprehensive nature of this multi-tiered transport strategy highlights the meticulous planning involved in hosting LEAP 2026. The coordination between Gulf Car, Makani, and Swvl is essential for creating a cohesive mobility ecosystem that addresses the diverse needs of the event's attendees. As the technology sector gathers in Riyadh from August 31 to September 3, 2026, the performance of these transportation providers will be a critical element in the successful execution of the event, demonstrating the capacity of the region to manage complex logistical operations for mega-events.

As the official transportation provider, Gulf Car is tasked with a significant operational mandate, facilitating the movement of attendees to the RECC Malham venue. This partnership is central to the event's logistical framework, ensuring that the primary transit routes are managed effectively. The emphasis on reliable external transportation reflects an understanding of the challenges associated with moving large volumes of people to a centralized location, making Gulf Car's role a vital component of the overall LEAP 2026 experience.

Within the venue, Makani's responsibility as the official internal shuttle provider addresses the specific need for efficient micro-mobility. The sprawling nature of the RECC Malham complex means that attendees will need to cover considerable distances to access various parts of the exhibition. By deploying internal shuttles, Makani aims to alleviate this challenge, providing a practical solution for navigating the extensive grounds. This service is designed to support the seamless transition of participants between different activities, enhancing their ability to participate fully in the event.

Looking Ahead

LEAP 2026 takes place from August 31 to September 3, 2026, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. As the event dates approach, the effectiveness of the transportation strategy will be tested by the influx of visitors. The success of Gulf Car, Makani, and Swvl in executing their respective roles will be a key factor in the overall attendee experience, influencing how participants perceive the logistical organization of the event.

The event organizers will likely monitor the performance of the transport network closely, making adjustments as needed to ensure smooth operations. The outcomes of this multi-tiered approach may also provide valuable insights for future large-scale events in the region, setting a benchmark for logistical planning and execution. The lessons learned from coordinating such a vast mobility network could influence how future exhibitions approach attendee transit.

articles.content_html:
At LEAP 2026 in Riyadh, a major shift from passive medical treatment to proactive health management was introduced as LIVE4WELL showcased its advanced LIVE4WELL AI health platform. This distinct healthtech announcement highlights practical, non-invasive AI applications in preventive healthcare, integrating multi-country testing technologies. The platform utilizes scientific assessment, digital monitoring, and personalized AI insights to provide users with a comprehensive understanding of their well-being.

The system's approach centers on delivering immediate, actionable health data through rapid screening modalities. By shifting the focus away from traditional reactive medicine, LIVE4WELL aims to empower individuals and healthcare providers with early detection capabilities. This proactive model is particularly relevant in the context of modern healthcare challenges, where early intervention can alter the trajectory of various conditions. The demonstration at LEAP 2026 underscored the potential to integrate directly into routine health assessments. This focus on prevention is central to the company's strategy, which emphasizes the value of early detection in improving long-term health trajectories. The integration of multi-country testing technologies further highlights the platform's broad applicability and ambition to serve diverse populations with distinct health profiles.

Rapid Retinal Screening for Risk Detection

A key feature of the newly showcased system is its AI retinal screening tool. This component uses fundus imaging to analyze retinal texture patterns, a method that provides a non-invasive window into the body's vascular and neurological health. According to the company's demonstrations, this screening tool delivers risk grading in just 30 seconds, a significant reduction in time compared to conventional diagnostic procedures.

The AI retinal screening is designed to identify and grade 55 distinct health risk factors. Among these are critical conditions such as brain degeneration and arteriosclerosis. The ability to detect markers for these diseases quickly and without invasive procedures represents a substantial advancement in preventive health AI. By analyzing the microvascular structures of the retina, the AI algorithm can identify subtle changes that may indicate the early stages of systemic diseases, allowing for timely intervention and management. The 30-second processing time for the retinal screening is a crucial operational metric, as it enables high-throughput assessments in clinical or community settings without causing significant delays or bottlenecks. This efficiency is vital for large-scale preventive health initiatives, where the volume of patients can often overwhelm traditional screening resources. The capability to grade 55 health risk factors from a single, non-invasive scan also reduces the need for multiple, disparate tests, streamlining the diagnostic process for both patients and healthcare providers.

Assessing Stress Resilience and Mental Health

In addition to physical health markers, the LIVE4WELL platform incorporates tools for evaluating mental well-being. The system includes a stress-resilience assessment that applies AI eye-tracking technology combined with visual stimulation. This component is designed to measure five specific mental health indices in a span of 90 seconds.

This digital health monitoring feature addresses the growing need for objective, accessible mental health assessments. By utilizing eye-tracking data in response to visual stimuli, the AI can evaluate physiological responses associated with stress and cognitive load. The integration of this mental health assessment alongside the physical screening tools provides a more holistic view of an individual's health status, aligning with the platform's goal of comprehensive proactive care. The 90-second duration for the stress-resilience assessment is notable for its brevity, offering a rapid alternative to lengthy psychological evaluations or self-reported questionnaires, which can sometimes be subjective or prone to bias. The use of eye-tracking and visual stimulation introduces a physiological dimension to mental health evaluation, capturing involuntary responses that may reveal underlying stress levels or cognitive fatigue that an individual might not consciously recognize or articulate. This objective measurement is critical for developing accurate, personalized mental health interventions and monitoring progress over time.

Implications for Healthcare in the Region

The introduction of the LIVE4WELL AI-driven healthcare platform at LEAP 2026 aligns with broader healthtech initiatives in Saudi Arabia and the Gulf Region. As healthcare systems globally and regionally seek to optimize resources and improve patient outcomes, technologies that facilitate early detection and preventive care are increasingly valuable. The non-invasive nature of these assessments could lower barriers to routine screening, potentially leading to earlier diagnoses and more effective management of chronic conditions. The deployment of such technologies supports the region's goals of modernizing healthcare infrastructure and integrating advanced digital solutions into everyday medical practice.

However, while the rapid screening capabilities demonstrated are promising, the broader implementation of such technologies will require integration into existing healthcare infrastructures. Questions remain regarding the large-scale deployment of these AI tools, the necessary regulatory approvals, and how the data generated will be managed and protected within clinical settings. The transition from a demonstration phase to widespread clinical application will be a critical next step for the platform. Healthcare providers will need to evaluate how these AI-generated insights can be directly incorporated into electronic health records and clinical workflows without adding administrative burden. Additionally, the accuracy and reliability of the AI algorithms must be continuously validated across diverse demographic groups to ensure equitable health outcomes and prevent algorithmic bias in risk grading. The successful adoption of the LIVE4WELL platform will depend on its ability to navigate these operational and regulatory challenges while demonstrating clear clinical utility and cost-effectiveness in real-world healthcare environments.

articles.content_html:
LEAP 2026 has officially opened in Riyadh with the launch of GameX Creative, a new dedicated zone celebrating gaming, storytelling, and digital culture. A major highlight of this zone is the debut of 'LEAP Into New Worlds', a custom Roblox obstacle course designed to engage the global gaming community with the event. The LEAP 2026 GameX Creative initiative represents a significant expansion of the conference's scope, moving beyond traditional enterprise technology to embrace the rapidly growing interactive entertainment sector. The integration of these elements reflects a broader recognition of gaming as a central component of the modern digital economy.

The Roblox experience allows players to race through a futuristic city, scale skyscrapers, and collect LEAP coins. This interactive environment represents a significant shift in how large-scale technology conferences engage with virtual audiences, extending the physical footprint of the Riyadh exhibition center into persistent digital spaces. The integration of such an experience signals an evolution in event programming, where physical attendance is complemented by gamified digital participation. By utilizing a platform with a massive global user base, the organizers are attempting to lower the barrier to entry for international audiences who cannot attend the physical event in Saudi Arabia. The 'LEAP Into New Worlds' activation serves as a bridge between the physical exhibition and the digital realm, offering a tangible example of the metaverse concepts often discussed at such conferences. This approach allows the event to maintain a continuous presence in the digital lives of its attendees, extending engagement beyond the four days of the physical exhibition.

Expanding the Digital Footprint

Additionally, GameX Creative features an ESL FACEIT esports racing simulator experience and hosts new game reveals. The inclusion of high-fidelity racing simulation provides attendees with hands-on exposure to competitive gaming hardware and software. By partnering with ESL FACEIT Group, the event organizers have secured a tier-one esports presence, which aligns with broader regional investments in the competitive gaming sector. The racing simulator is designed to showcase the technical capabilities of modern esports setups, offering a tangible demonstration of the hardware required for professional competition. This hands-on approach allows attendees to experience the level of performance expected by professional gamers, highlighting the technological advancements driving the esports industry forward. The presence of such hardware also serves as a focal point for discussions surrounding the infrastructure required to support a thriving esports ecosystem.

The decision to host new game reveals during the event further establishes the conference as a viable platform for industry announcements, competing with established gaming conventions. This approach broadens the appeal of the event beyond traditional enterprise technology and telecommunications sectors, attracting developers, publishers, and enthusiasts. The inclusion of these reveals suggests an ambition to position Riyadh not just as a consumer market, but as a critical node in the global gaming industry's promotional circuit. By providing a stage for these announcements, LEAP 2026 aims to capture the attention of the global gaming press and community, further amplifying its reach and influence. The ability to attract major game reveals is a strong indicator of the event's growing prestige within the international gaming community.

Strategic Industry Focus

This announcement represents a significant expansion of LEAP's focus on the gaming and immersive technology sectors, providing interactive and engaging platforms for attendees and virtual participants alike. The development of GameX Creative aligns with the growing emphasis on the digital economy within Saudi Arabia and the wider MENA region. As investments in gaming infrastructure and content creation increase, dedicated event zones serve as critical hubs for networking, investment, and talent acquisition. The presence of major international entities alongside regional stakeholders creates an environment conducive to strategic partnerships and business development. This convergence of international expertise and local ambition is central to the region's broader economic diversification strategies. The zone acts as a catalyst for local developers and entrepreneurs to connect with global industry leaders, fostering knowledge transfer and collaboration.

The collaboration between Informa Tech, Roblox Corporation, and ESL FACEIT Group highlights the intersection of traditional event management, user-generated content platforms, and professional esports organizations. This convergence is indicative of the multifaceted nature of the modern gaming industry, where distinct sectors increasingly overlap to create comprehensive entertainment ecosystems. The physical space allocated to GameX Creative within the broader exhibition demonstrates a commitment to treating gaming as a primary pillar of the technological landscape, rather than a niche interest. This dedicated zone provides a focused environment for industry professionals to discuss the future of interactive entertainment, from technological innovations to evolving business models. The integration of these diverse elements underscores the complexity of the modern gaming ecosystem, which encompasses everything from casual mobile gaming to highly competitive professional esports.

Evaluating the Long-Term Impact

While the launch of GameX Creative and the 'LEAP Into New Worlds' Roblox experience marks a notable expansion, the long-term impact on attendee engagement and virtual participation remains to be seen. The success of the Roblox integration will likely be measured by sustained player activity and the conversion of virtual participants into active followers of the event's broader technology themes. The challenge lies in ensuring that the digital experience offers meaningful value beyond a simple novelty, encouraging users to return and explore further content related to the conference. The ability to translate in-game engagement into tangible interest in the event's core technological discussions will be a critical metric for evaluating the success of this initiative. Organizers must determine whether the gamified elements effectively communicate the overarching themes of the conference or merely serve as a distraction.

Furthermore, the effectiveness of the ESL FACEIT racing simulator in driving interest in regional esports initiatives will require ongoing assessment. As LEAP 2026 runs from August 31 to September 3 in Riyadh, the initial reception of these new features will provide valuable insights into the future trajectory of gaming-focused programming within major technology conferences. The feedback gathered from both physical attendees and digital participants will be crucial in refining the GameX Creative concept for future iterations, determining whether this hybrid approach to event programming can be successfully scaled and sustained. Organizers will need to carefully analyze participation data to understand which elements resonated most strongly with the audience. This data-driven approach will be essential for optimizing future investments in interactive event programming.

articles.content_html:
Riyadh — Saudi proptech startup [Ghanem][1] has secured $7.1 million from the Al-Romaih Group to advance its digital fractional real estate ownership platform. Established in 2025 by Saleh Al-Ghamdi and Amr Essam, the company currently operates within the Regulatory Sandbox of the Saudi Real Estate General Authority (REGA). The capital injection is intended to reduce entry barriers for both individual and institutional investors in the domestic property market, offering transparent and flexible investment avenues. This strategic development directly supports Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 objectives concerning digital transformation and the diversification of real estate assets. The newly acquired funds will be deployed to broaden product offerings, upgrade technological infrastructure, and expand the base of real estate investment across the Kingdom, representing a notable step toward democratizing property investment in Saudi Arabia.

The fractional real estate ownership model divides property assets into smaller, accessible shares, lowering the financial threshold for investors who previously faced substantial capital requirements. Operating under the REGA Regulatory Sandbox allows Ghanem to test this model within a structured, overseen environment while refining its core product offerings. The startup specializes in providing these fractional ownership tools, and the capital will accelerate product development and market expansion.

Democratizing Property Investment

The Saudi real estate market has historically demanded high capital outlays, restricting access primarily to wealthy individuals and large institutions. By introducing a fractional ownership structure, Ghanem aims to open this lucrative asset class to a wider demographic. This approach enables participation in smaller increments, reducing the financial burden on individual investors and allowing them to diversify their portfolios with assets that were previously inaccessible. This shift is particularly relevant in a market characterized by steadily rising property values that often outpace average income growth. The ability to invest smaller amounts of capital into real estate assets provides a new avenue for wealth generation for a segment of the population that has historically been excluded from direct property ownership.

Furthermore, Ghanem's digital-first platform introduces efficiency and transparency to property transactions. Investors gain access to detailed property information, real-time investment tracking, and streamlined execution processes. This emphasis on transparency is designed to build trust by providing clear visibility into property valuations, rental yields, and associated costs, which is essential for mitigating typical real estate investment risks. The digital nature of the platform also caters to a younger, tech-savvy generation of investors who expect seamless, accessible financial services. By providing a user-friendly interface and comprehensive data, Ghanem seeks to empower investors to make informed decisions regarding their property portfolios.

Regulatory Framework and Compliance

Ghanem's integration into the REGA Regulatory Sandbox is central to its operational strategy. This environment enables the startup to align its digital fractional ownership platform with existing regulatory standards while seeking to offer flexible investment opportunities. The $7.1 million capital injection will support ongoing platform development to ensure compliance with the requirements of both regulators and investors. The sandbox provides a controlled setting where innovative business models can be tested without the immediate burden of full regulatory compliance, allowing the company to identify potential risks and develop robust frameworks in collaboration with authorities. This collaborative approach between the private sector and regulatory bodies is crucial for fostering innovation while maintaining market stability and protecting consumer interests.

Operating within the REGA framework also lends legitimacy to Ghanem's platform, as investors are more likely to trust a service operating under the oversight of a recognized regulatory body. This oversight ensures adherence to best practices in consumer protection, data privacy, and anti-money laundering. As the platform matures and eventually transitions out of the sandbox, the foundational compliance established during this phase will be critical for navigating the broader financial sector's regulatory landscape. The insights gained from operating within the sandbox will also inform future regulatory frameworks for fractional real estate ownership in Saudi Arabia, potentially paving the way for wider adoption of this investment model.

Vision 2030 and Market Expansion

The initiative to lower entry thresholds for investors aligns with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 goals for digital transformation and economic diversification. By facilitating broader participation in property investment, Ghanem contributes to the growth and maturation of the real estate sector, a key component in diversifying the national economy away from traditional oil revenues. The government's prioritization of digital technologies to enhance efficiency and innovation is reflected in Ghanem's approach, demonstrating how technology can disrupt traditional business models. The success of such platforms could encourage further innovation within the Saudi proptech ecosystem, attracting additional investment and talent to the sector.

The capital from Al-Romaih Group will be allocated toward refining platform features and expanding market presence. This expansion may involve geographic growth within the Kingdom and the introduction of new investment products, such as commercial properties or specialized residential developments, to cater to diverse investor preferences. However, the successful scaling of this model will depend on Ghanem's ability to transition from the regulatory sandbox to full compliance, as well as its capacity to maintain transparency and security as user volumes increase. Key questions remain regarding the liquidity of fractional shares in the secondary market and how the platform will handle potential disputes among fractional owners. The integration of advanced technologies, such as blockchain for tokenization or artificial intelligence for personalized recommendations, could further solidify its market position, though these remain potential future developments rather than immediate realities.
